newsitem.title: UK: Firecrest to delist from AIM on October 2.
newsitem.headline: Firecrest to delist from AIM on October 2.

text.p: Firecrest Group Plc said its shares would be delisted from London's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) effective 0730 GMT on October 2 after its nominated adviser and nominated broker resigned on September 2.
The marketing services group said discussions which could lead to an offer for the company, first publicised on August 30, were continuing.

Firecrest also said that it had issued high court proceedings with other group and associated companies against two former employees, Steve McVickers and Oscar Jenkins, and against Associated Newspapers and one of its journalists, Tom Winnifrith.
The other companies starting high court proceedings are Nethead Limited, Global On-Line Directory Limited and Netex Network Communication Corp.

The proceedings are for damages resulting from allegedly defamatory statements Firecrest said were made by McVickers and Jenkins and for allegedly defamatory articles about Firecrest published by the Evening Standard, Firecrest said.
Firecrest said if a recommended offer were not made for the company, it would try to provide alternative trading facilities for its securities through Ofex.
